newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares snap out of misery, end with gains.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares snap out of misery, end with gains.

text.p: Greek shares regained momentum after edging lower in early trade, helped by the sale of a 12 percent stake in Heracles by National Bank which boosted market sentiment, brokers said.

"The corporate news on the sale of a good stake in Heracles by National Bank helped market sentiment and stocks rebounded. Let's not forget a key factor: the equities market in Greece has strong fundamentals," said broker Yannis Kalogerakis at ABN AMRO Axias Securities.
"I expect better days by year-end. The market saw a large block trade in Ergo Bank go through and this helped banks to settle with gains," he said.
Italy's Concretum agreed to buy a 12 percent stake in Heracles Cements for 32.23 billion drachmas or 5,320 drachmas a share from National Bank. Heracles closed up 160 drachmas at 3,160.
Selling pressure on Thursday, sparked by jitters from Ergobank's 5.29 percent plunge which pulled the market 1.69 percent lower subsided on Friday helping the banking sector climb 1.15 percent.
Ergo Bank has rescheduled a shareholders meeting for December 17 after a proposal by one of its shareholders, Lazaros Efremoglou, who opposed its planned 27.3 billion drachma rights issue.

The Athens general share index closed up 0.60 percent or 5.37 points higher at 906.02 from Thursday's 900.65 close after opening at 900.78. Turnover jumped to 10.61 billion drachmas on volume of 2.5 million shares.
